category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Childhood renal cancer associated with WAGR syndrome and deletions in 11p13 involves mutations in the [___] gene.
back:
• WT1 gene.
• Associated with aniridia and gonadoblastomas.
• Usually affects children before age 5.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A female child presents with constant urine dribbling despite having normal, controlled voiding episodes. Name the likely anomaly.
back:
• Ectopic ureter.
• Caused by a second ureteric bud opening below the bladder.
• In females, opens into the vagina, vestibule, or urethra.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Describe the developmental failure that results in a urachal fistula.
back:
• Persistence of the entire allantois lumen.
• Creates direct communication between the bladder and umbilicus.
• Clinically causes urine to leak from the navel.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Distinguish between a urachal cyst and a urachal sinus regarding their clinical presentation.
back:
• Urachal Cyst: Fluid-filled cavity in a partially obliterated allantois (internal).
• Urachal Sinus: Blind-ending pocket opening at the umbilicus.
• Both represent incomplete allantois regression.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Characterize the histological finding of a Multicystic Dysplastic Kidney.
back:
• Numerous ducts surrounded by undifferentiated cells.
• Nephrons fail to develop.
• Ureteric bud fails to branch; collecting ducts never form.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: In a horseshoe kidney, the ascent of the fused lower poles is arrested at the level of the [___] artery.
back: The inferior mesenteric artery. This occurs because the kidneys fuse at their lower poles while still in the pelvis and get trapped during their cranial migration.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A neonate presents with flattened facial features, clubbed feet, and respiratory distress. Prenatal ultrasound showed severe oligohydramnios. Identify the underlying developmental sequence.
back: Potter sequence. It is primarily caused by bilateral renal agenesis or lack of urine production, leading to oligohydramnios and subsequent fetal compression and pulmonary hypoplasia.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Explain how a failure in the signaling between GDNF (produced by metanephric mesoderm) and the RET receptor (on the ureteric bud) results in renal agenesis.
back: The interaction is essential for the ureteric bud to branch and grow. Without this signal, the bud fails to induce the metanephric blastema to form nephrons.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A child presents with massive bilateral renal enlargement and hepatic fibrosis, whereas an adult presents with hypertension and berry aneurysms. Contrast the renal cyst origins in these two conditions.
back: ARPKD (childhood): Cysts form exclusively from collecting ducts. ADPKD (adult): Cysts form from all segments of the nephron. Both are considered ciliopathies affecting ciliary protein function.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Identify the embryological remnant resulting in a urachal fistula where urine leaks through the umbilicus.
back: Persistence of the lumen of the allantois. Normally, the allantois obliterates to form a thick fibrous cord called the urachus (median umbilical ligament).

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: WAGR syndrome, which includes Wilms' tumor and aniridia, is caused by a microdeletion on chromosome [___].
back: 11p13. This deletion affects both the WT1 gene (linked to renal tumors) and the PAX6 gene (linked to aniridia), which are located close together.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A young girl presents with constant dribbling of urine despite normal voiding patterns. This clinical finding most likely suggests an ectopic ureter opening into the [___].
back: Vagina, urethra, or vestibule. This occurs when a second ureteric bud develops or if the ureteric bud fails to separate normally from the mesonephric duct.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Relate the development of the definitive bladder trigone to its dual embryological origins.
back: The trigone is initially formed by the mesodermal mesonephric ducts being absorbed into the bladder wall. Eventually, this mesodermal lining is replaced by endodermal epithelium from the urogenital sinus.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Contrast the pelvic kidney from a normal kidney regarding its vascular supply and position.
back: A pelvic kidney fails to ascend and remains near the common iliac artery. Its blood supply is derived from adjacent vessels like the common iliac or lower aorta.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Specify the embryonic structure that gives rise to the prostatic and membranous parts of the male urethra.
back: The pelvic part of the urogenital sinus. This endodermal structure also gives rise to the prostate gland via epithelial outgrowths into the surrounding mesenchyme.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: During the ascent of the definitive kidney from the pelvic to the abdominal region, the fusion of the lower poles creates a horseshoe kidney which is arrested by the [___] artery.
back:
• Inferior mesenteric artery
• Occurs in 1/600 births
• Kidneys remain at the level of lower lumbar vertebrae

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A newborn presents with flattened facial features, clubbed feet, and severe respiratory distress. The pregnancy was complicated by profound oligohydramnios. What is the most likely developmental diagnosis?
back:
• Potter sequence (Bilateral renal agenesis)
• Lack of urine production causes oligohydramnios
• Leads to uterine compression and pulmonary hypoplasia

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Explain the role of the GDNF/RET signaling pathway in the initiation of renal development.
back:
• GDNF is produced by metanephric mesenchyme
• Binds to RET receptors on the ureteric bud
• Stimulates ureteric bud branching and growth

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Contrast the clinical presentation and cyst origin between Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD) and Autosomal Dominant Polycystic Kidney Disease (ADPKD).
back:
• ARPKD: Cysts from collecting ducts; renal failure in infancy
• ADPKD: Cysts from all nephron segments; renal failure in adulthood
• Both are ciliopathies (cilia protein mutations)

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Identify the components of the WAGR syndrome associated with microdeletions of the WT1 and PAX6 genes.
back:
• W: Wilms' tumor
• A: Aniridia
• G: Gonadoblastoma (genitourinary anomalies)
• R: Mental retardation

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: If the lumen of the intraembryonic allantois persists throughout its length, it results in a clinical condition called a [___], characterized by urine drainage from the umbilicus.
back:
• Urachal fistula
• Represents a direct communication between bladder and umbilicus
• Result of failure of allantois obliteration

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A young girl presents with constant urinary dribbling despite normal voiding patterns. Embryologically, how does an ectopic ureter explain this presentation?
back:
• Formation of two ureteric buds
• One bud shifts caudally with the mesonephric duct
• Enters vagina, vestibule, or urethra below the sphincter

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Describe the mechanism by which the ureteric bud and metanephric blastema interact to form the definitive kidney.
back:
• Reciprocal induction: Bud induces mesenchyme to form nephrons
• Mesenchyme induces bud to branch (collecting system)
• Failure of interaction causes renal agenesis/dysplasia

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Contrast the embryological origin of the bladder trigone's mucosal lining with that of the rest of the urinary bladder.
back:
• Trigone: Initially Mesoderm (from mesonephric ducts)
• Remainder: Endoderm (from urogenital sinus)
• Note: Trigone mesoderm is eventually replaced by endoderm

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Mention the primary gene mutation and chromosome location typically associated with the development of Wilms' tumor.
back:
• WT1 gene mutation
• Chromosome 11p13
• Often involves failure of mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: The permanent kidney, or metanephros, begins its development during the [___] week of gestation from the intermediate mesoderm.
back:
- Fifth week
- Derived from metanephric blastema and ureteric bud
- Represents the definitive renal system

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: A newborn presents with flattened facies, clubbed feet, and respiratory distress. Ultrasound confirms bilateral renal agenesis. Identify this clinical sequence and its primary cause.
back:
- Potter sequence
- Caused by oligohydramnios (low amniotic fluid)
- Results from lack of fetal urine contribution to the amniotic cavity

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: Describe the inductive signaling pathway between the metanephric mesenchyme and the ureteric bud involving the WT1 gene.
back:
- WT1 makes mesenchyme competent to respond to induction
- Mesenchyme secretes GDNF and HGF
- Growth factors bind RET and MET receptors on the ureteric bud to stimulate branching

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: A child is diagnosed with Wilms tumor. Contrast the genetic basis and clinical features of WAGR syndrome versus Denys-Drash syndrome.
back:
- WAGR: Microdeletion (WT1 and PAX6); includes aniridia and intellectual disability
- Denys-Drash: WT1 mutation; includes renal failure and ambiguous genitalia
- Both involve high risk of nephroblastoma

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: List the specific derivatives of the ureteric bud within the definitive urinary system.
back:
- Ureter and renal pelvis
- Major and minor calyces
- Approximately 1 to 3 million collecting tubules

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: During the development of the urinary bladder, the mesodermal [___] is formed by the incorporation of the mesonephric ducts into the posterior wall.
back:
- Trigone of the bladder
- Initially mesodermal but later replaced by endodermal epithelium
- Located between the ureteric orifices and the internal urethral orifice

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: A routine prenatal scan identifies a 'horseshoe kidney'. Explain the embryological basis and identify the vessel that limits its cephalad migration.
back:
- Lower poles of kidneys fuse in the pelvis
- Ascent is arrested by the Inferior Mesenteric Artery (IMA)
- Kidney remains at lower lumbar level

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: Explain how the metanephric mesenchyme undergoes mesenchymal-to-epithelial transition (MET) to form renal tubules.
back:
- Ureteric bud secretes WNT9B and WNT6
- Upregulates PAX2 (condensation) and WNT4 (epithelialization) in mesenchyme
- Extracellular matrix shifts to laminin and type IV collagen

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: Distinguish between the three kidney systems (Pronephros, Mesonephros, Metanephros) based on their functional status and location.
back:
- Pronephros: Cervical, vestigial/non-functional
- Mesonephros: Thoracic/Lumbar, briefly functional; forms Wolffian duct
- Metanephros: Sacral/Pelvic, forms the permanent adult kidney

category: Describe development of intermediate mesoderm and its derivatives
front: Identify the structure that divides the cloaca into the urogenital sinus and the anal canal.
back:
- Urorectal septum
- Mesodermal layer between the hindgut and allantois
- Tip forms the perineal body

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: In a horseshoe kidney, the upward migration of the fused lower poles is prevented by the [___] artery.
back:
• Inferior mesenteric artery (IMA)
• Occurs at the L3 vertebral level
• Results in the kidneys being lower than normal.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A neonate presents with massively enlarged kidneys and rapid renal failure. Histology confirms cysts localized strictly to the collecting ducts. Identify the condition.
back:
• Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD)
• Caused by PKHD1 gene mutations
• Associated with hepatic fibrosis and biliary cysts.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Explain the embryological mechanism that leads to an ectopic ureter opening into the vagina or vestibule.
back:
• Development of two ureteric buds
• The abnormal bud moves caudally with the mesonephric duct
• Enters the urethra, vagina, or vestibule instead of the bladder.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A 4-year-old child presents with an abdominal mass, aniridia, and intellectual disability. Contrast the genetic cause of this presentation with isolated Wilms' tumor.
back:
• Presentation: WAGR syndrome (11p13 microdeletion)
• Involves PAX6 (aniridia) and WT1 genes
• Isolated Wilms': Primarily point mutations in WT1 gene.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Identify the clinical presentation and anatomical status of a urachal fistula.
back:
• Presentation: Continuous leakage of urine from the umbilicus
• Anatomy: Complete patency of the allantoic lumen
• Connects the bladder lumen directly to the exterior.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A kidney that remains in the pelvic cavity near the common iliac artery due to failure of ascent is termed a [___].
back:
• Pelvic kidney
• Results from failure to 'climb' from the sacral region
• Usually functional but may cause obstetric complications.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: An infant presents with a blind-ending pocket at the umbilicus that intermittently drains serous fluid but does not leak urine. Identify the anomaly.
back:
• Urachal sinus
• Cephalic end of allantois remains patent
• Separated from the bladder by the obliterated urachus.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Describe the developmental failure that results in a multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK).
back:
• Ureteric bud fails to branch correctly
• Failure of induction between bud and metanephric blastema
• Nephrons never form; replaced by undifferentiated stroma.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Distinguish between ARPKD and ADPKD regarding the segment of the nephron involved in cyst formation.
back:
• ARPKD: Cysts form exclusively from collecting ducts
• ADPKD: Cysts form from all segments of the nephron
• ADPKD is more common (1/500 vs 1/5,000).

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Specify the embryological error that results in a duplicated or 'bifid' ureter.
back:
• Early splitting of the ureteric bud
• Can be partial (Y-shaped) or complete duplication
• Results in two renal pelves on the same side.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: In a horseshoe kidney, the ascent of the joined kidneys is arrested by the [___] artery.
back:
- Inferior mesenteric artery (IMA).
- The kidneys usually fuse at their lower poles.
- The resulting U-shaped organ remains trapped at the level of the lower lumbar vertebrae.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A neonate presents with flattened facial features (Potter facies), club feet, and severe pulmonary hypoplasia. These findings are most likely secondary to [___] caused by bilateral renal agenesis.
back:
- Oligohydramnios.
- Lack of fetal urine production reduces amniotic fluid volume.
- Uterine compression leads to characteristic physical deformities and prevents normal lung development.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Explain the embryological mechanism leading to a duplicated ureter or a bifid ureter.
back:
- Early splitting of the ureteric bud.
- Partial splitting results in a bifid ureter.
- Complete duplication occurs if two independent ureteric buds arise from the mesonephric duct.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Contrast the clinical onset and cyst origin between Autosomal Dominant (ADPKD) and Autosomal Recessive Polycystic Kidney Disease (ARPKD).
back:
- ADPKD: Adult onset; cysts form from all nephron segments.
- ARPKD: Infantile onset; cysts form specifically from collecting ducts.
- ARPKD is generally more progressive, often leading to early renal failure.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Identify the three primary types of urachal anomalies resulting from the failure of the allantois lumen to obliterate.
back:
- Urachal Fistula: Patent lumen connecting bladder to umbilicus.
- Urachal Cyst: Isolated fluid-filled pocket within the urachal remnant.
- Urachal Sinus: Blind pocket opening at the umbilicus.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Wilms tumor, a common renal cancer in children under 5, is primarily associated with mutations in the [___] gene located on chromosome 11p13.
back:
- WT1 (Wilms Tumor 1) gene.
- This gene is essential for mesenchyme-to-epithelial transition.
- Mutations may occur as part of WAGR or Denys-Drash syndromes.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A female infant is found to have urine continuously dripping from the vagina despite normal voiding patterns. This clinical presentation suggests an [___].
back:
- Ectopic Ureter.
- Results from an abnormal ureteric bud position.
- In females, the ureter bypasses the bladder sphincter and opens into the vagina or vestibule.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Describe how the mesonephric ducts contribute to the formation of the urinary bladder trigone.
back:
- Caudal portions of mesonephric ducts are absorbed into the bladder wall.
- This forms the trigone, which is initially mesodermal.
- The mesodermal lining is eventually replaced by endodermal epithelium.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Distinguish the adult derivatives of the ureteric bud from those of the metanephric mesoderm (blastema).
back:
- Ureteric Bud: Ureter, renal pelvis, calyces, and collecting tubules.
- Metanephric Blastema: Nephrons (Bowman’s capsule, proximal/distal convoluted tubules, and loop of Henle).

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Specify the anatomical consequence of the kidney failing to 'ascend' from its initial sacral position.
back:
- Pelvic Kidney.
- The kidney remains near the common iliac artery.
- While ectopic in location, these kidneys often function normally unless obstruction occurs.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: During the ascent of the kidneys, the fusion of the lower poles results in a horseshoe kidney, which is trapped under the [___] artery.
back:
• Inferior mesenteric artery.
• Occurs because the fused lower pole is unable to pass the origin of the artery at the aorta.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A 4-year-old child presents with a large abdominal mass and absence of the iris (aniridia). Identify the likely mutated gene and associated syndrome.
back:
• WT1 gene mutation.
• WAGR Syndrome.
• Includes Wilms’ tumor, Aniridia, Gonadoblastoma, and intellectual disability.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Explain how an ectopic ureter originates during development when two ureteric buds are present.
back:
• One bud enters the bladder normally.
• The abnormal bud migrates caudally with the mesonephric duct.
• Drains into the vagina, vestibule, or prostatic urethra.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Contrast the segment of the nephron involved and the typical age of renal failure onset between ARPKD and ADPKD.
back:
• ARPKD: Cysts in collecting ducts only; failure in infancy/childhood.
• ADPKD: Cysts in all nephron segments; failure in adulthood.
• ADPKD is more common but less aggressive.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Describe the structural failure that leads to the formation of a multicystic dysplastic kidney.
back:
• Ureteric bud fails to branch.
• Collecting ducts never form.
• Nephrons fail to develop, leaving undifferentiated tissue and numerous cysts.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: If the lumen of the allantois fails to obliterate during development, a [___] is formed, allowing urine to drain from the umbilicus.
back:
• Urachal fistula.
• Result of a completely patent allantois.
• Direct communication between bladder and umbilicus.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A neonate presents with ambiguous genitalia and rapid-onset renal failure. Histology confirms a Wilms' tumor. Name this specific clinical constellation.
back:
• Denys-Drash Syndrome.
• Characterized by renal failure, ambiguous genitalia, and Wilms' tumor.
• Linked to WT1 gene mutations.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Explain the developmental mechanism resulting in a unilateral pelvic kidney.
back:
• Failure of the kidney to ascend from the sacral region.
• Remnant position near the common iliac artery.
• Caused by failure of the metanephros to shift cranially.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Distinguish between a urachal cyst and a urachal sinus based on their persistence pattern.
back:
• Urachal Cyst: Localized patent area of allantois; no external openings.
• Urachal Sinus: Distal part of allantois remains patent; opens at the umbilicus.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Identify the embryological tissue layer that initially forms the trigone of the bladder before it is replaced.
back:
• Mesoderm.
• Derived from the incorporation of the mesonephric ducts.
• Eventually replaced by endodermal epithelium.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: In a horseshoe kidney, the cranial ascent of the fused lower poles is halted at the L3 level by the [___] artery.
back:
- Inferior mesenteric artery (IMA).
- The kidneys are trapped beneath the origin of this vessel.
- Typically found in the lower lumbar region.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A newborn presents with urine constantly leaking from the umbilicus. Identify the underlying embryological defect.
back:
Urachal fistula.
- Caused by the total failure of the allantois lumen to obliterate.
- Establishes a direct communication between the bladder and umbilicus.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Explain the developmental failure leading to multicystic dysplastic kidney (MCDK).
back:
- Failure of the ureteric bud to branch.
- Collecting ducts never form, leading to involution of nephrons.
- Renal tissue is replaced by numerous cysts and undifferentiated cells.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Contrast Denys-Drash syndrome with WAGR syndrome regarding their unique clinical features.
back:
- Denys-Drash: Renal failure and ambiguous genitalia.
- WAGR: Aniridia, gonadoblastoma, and intellectual disability.
- Both involve mutations/deletions of the WT1 gene on chromosome 11.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Identify the embryological event that results in an ectopic ureter opening into the vagina or vestibule.
back:
- Development of two ureteric buds from the mesonephric duct.
- The abnormal bud migrates caudally with the mesonephric duct.
- Results in a low entrance into urogenital sinus derivatives.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A kidney that fails to pass through the arterial fork formed by the umbilical arteries remains near the common iliac artery, a condition termed [___].
back:
Pelvic kidney (Ectopic kidney).
- Occurs when the kidney fails to ascend to the lumbar region.
- Usually functional despite the abnormal pelvic location.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A child presents with a localized, midline cystic mass between the umbilicus and the bladder apex, with no external drainage. State the diagnosis.
back:
Urachal cyst.
- Caused by partial persistence of the allantois lumen.
- Only a small, isolated section remains patent while ends obliterate.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Describe the mechanistic difference in ureteric bud development that leads to partial versus complete duplication of the ureter.
back:
- Partial duplication: Early splitting of a single ureteric bud.
- Complete duplication: Development of two separate ureteric buds from the mesonephric duct.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Contrast the anatomical communication of a urachal sinus with that of a urachal fistula.
back:
- Urachal Sinus: Only the upper end remains patent, communicating with the umbilicus.
- Urachal Fistula: Entire lumen is patent, communicating between the bladder and umbilicus.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Identify the mesodermal structure that divides the cloaca into the urogenital sinus and the anal canal.
back:
Urorectal septum.
- Separates the anterior urogenital sinus from the posterior anorectal canal.
- The tip forms the perineal body.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: In a horseshoe kidney, the inferior poles of the kidneys typically fuse in the pelvis; their subsequent cranially-directed ascent is characteristically arrested by the [___] artery.
back:
• Inferior mesenteric artery (IMA).
• The fused kidneys are trapped at the level of lower lumbar vertebrae (L3-L5).
• Ureters typically arise from the anterior surface of the fused organ.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Explain the embryological mechanism that causes an ectopic ureter to drain into the vagina or vestibule in females rather than the urinary bladder.
back:
• Cause: Formation of two ureteric buds from a single mesonephric duct.
• Migration: The abnormal bud moves caudally with the mesonephric duct.
• Outcome: It bypasses the bladder trigone to enter urogenital sinus derivatives (vagina/urethra).

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: Contrast the anatomical location and vascular supply of a pelvic kidney with that of a normally ascended kidney.
back:
• Position: Pelvic kidney remains near the common iliac artery; normal kidney reaches the upper lumbar region.
• Blood Supply: Pelvic kidneys receive blood from nearby common iliac or distal aorta; normal kidneys receive renal arteries.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
front: A neonate presents with urine leaking from the umbilicus during crying and periumbilical dermatitis. Identify the embryological anomaly and the structure that failed to obliterate.
back:
• Diagnosis: Urachal fistula.
• Embryological structure: Allantois.
• Pathophysiology: Persistent patency of the entire allantoic lumen, creating a direct communication between the bladder apex and umbilicus.

category: List and describe the common congenital anomalies of kidney, urinary bladder and urethra
coreConcept: Glandular Derivatives of the Urogenital Sinus
front: Outline the developmental steps that lead to the formation of the prostate gland in males versus the paraurethral glands in females.
back:
• Step 1: Proliferation of endodermal epithelium from the prostatic urethra.
• Step 2: Epithelial buds penetrate the surrounding mesenchyme.
• Result: Buds form the prostate (male) or urethral/paraurethral glands (female).
